rows.label: Consumption per person of refugees in their first year and people seeking asylum in the UK, as a share of the UK survey average

source.title: GOV.UK, Asylum support: what you'll get
source.quote: You'll usually get £49.18 for each person in your household.

rows.explainer: People seeking asylum live on £49.18 a week (about £2,560 a year) in self-catered housing, or £9.95 a week in hotels with meals provided, with the accommodation provided by the Home Office; with the housing and meals at their value, a few thousand pounds a year, under a fifth of the UK survey average (@united_kingdom.consumption_per_person_2024 × @survey_consumption.survey_to_na_gbr, about $27,000). Newly recognised and resettled refugees in their first year live on Universal Credit (£393 a month for a single adult over 25 in 2024/25) with council-arranged or temporary housing, a little more. 18%, range 10% to 30%. Read by every model of help to refugees and people seeking asylum in the UK, so they value the same people the same way.

rows.label: Share of England's people living under an elected mayor once the 2028 mayors are elected

source.title: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Secretary of State's annual report on English devolution 2024-25
source.quote: As of May 2025, 51.49% of England is covered by mayoral devolution.
source.note: Low: today's mayoral coverage. High: the report's 77% ('just over 44 million people', para 6.3) once the Devolution Priority Programme's agreements are in place, which counts non-mayoral authorities too. Best 65%: the six Devolution Priority Programme areas, about 9 million people (Cheshire and Warrington and Cumbria first elect mayors in May 2027; Greater Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk, Hampshire and the Solent, and Sussex and Brighton in May 2028), add about 15 points of England's 58.6 million to today's 51.5% (66.5%), less the few councils in those areas that stay outside a mayoral authority: 65%; the non-mayoral foundation authorities make up the rest of the 77%.

rows.explainer: About two thirds of England's people (51% to 77%) will elect a mayor from 2028: the people a change in how mayors are elected reaches.
